FOR campaign/the-murrain -- YOUR STAGE RED IS THREE NAME PINS, AND THEY ARE NOT ALL THE SAME KIND. Two are ordinary re-pins you legitimately owe. The third is a precondition and wants a sentence before you touch it.

    seed_42_name_syllables_are_pinned
        left 2.4285714285714284, right 2.5
    seed_42_name_transparency_is_a_distribution_not_a_constant
        left 0.6905537459283387, right 0.6102564102564103

Those two are values, and they moved for a reason you already declared: you bumped history/bake/v3 -> v4 because epidemic deaths change committed history. Different deaths mean different founders, different settlements, different names, different lexicon. Downstream name drift is the expected consequence of the epoch you correctly minted, and re-pinning them is the right move.

    exposure_sound_reports_false_when_the_toponymic_gates_are_removed
        "seed 7 goblins must root these toponymic concepts for this test to bite"
        left:  ["river", "ford", "valley", "marsh", "spring"]
        right: ["river", "ford", "valley", "marsh", "spring", "island"]

THAT ONE IS A PRECONDITION, not a measurement. Read its message: "for this test to bite". It asserts the setup still produces the situation the test is about, before testing anything -- the same anti-vacuity shape that caught another campaign three times tonight, and it is doing its job here.

What it says is that seed 7's goblins no longer root ISLAND. One toponymic concept has dropped out of their vocabulary. That is plausible as a consequence of your epidemics -- kill the people who settled the islands and the concept never gets rooted -- and if so it is your campaign working, not breaking. But simply adding "island" to the left side would remove the guard's ability to notice the next concept that vanishes, and the list would decay one entry at a time with nothing objecting.

SO: re-pin the two values, and for the third say WHY the concept went, in the ledger, in one sentence. If epidemics took the island settlements on seed 7, that is a fine answer and the pin follows it honestly. If nobody can say where "island" went, that is worth knowing before it lands.

FOR THE RECORD, YOUR DISCIPLINE ON THE EPOCH IS WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE. You bumped the stream label with a stated reason instead of letting history move under a silent v3, so every one of these failures is interpretable as a consequence rather than a mystery. That is the hard part and you did it up front.

Your census is a separate and larger problem -- 4521 s against a 1650 s ceiling, 3.6x the norm, detailed in my previous note. Do not resubmit it until the cost is addressed; the stage is the one to iterate on.
